context_review.use: PayloadHeader derives Serialize/Deserialize and owns schema_id: SchemaId and schema_version; header decode is the deserialization caller context.
Text inspection first borrows the raw envelope/payload and then strictly decodes PayloadHeader; header SchemaId ownership is separate from the borrowed payload.

Public versioned loading routes text to load_text_versioned; envelope schema/version are validated before old payload becomes Value; load_migrated_value then runs the chain and decodes the target type.
migrate_value validates the complete target chain and invokes each step for from_version..target_version; input 1/target 2 invokes fixture step 1.
The fixture chain must have every adjacent step from version 0 through target 2; this validation occurs before invoking the selected migration callback.
dev profile has no overflow-check override; test profile lines 82-84 likewise do not override it; shipping separately sets overflow-checks=false and is not the test-only fixture path.

parse_integer keeps positive integer significands in u64 until actual overflow; parse_number emits ParserNumber::U64 for a positive integer, so the exact maximum is representable as an unsigned JSON integer.
Number::as_u64 returns the positive-integer u64 value; u64::MAX therefore passes the fixture helper's as_u64 guard.

review_conclusions: SchemaId static construction borrows static text; dynamic conversion/deserialization owns validated text. The added lifetime sentence is consistent with Cow ownership and loader header ownership.

VersionedSchema supplies stable schema/current version and an ordered whole-chain migration contract; loader format/schema/version checks precede callbacks, and domain validation remains caller-owned.
Existing complete documentation covers clear module/trait/schema tests. Added fixture docs describe shared test scope, object input/return and ordering; originals remain exact.

No new FFI, dynamic registration or macro-generated behavioral entry exists in these five formal sources. The 38 cross-tree trait implementations are a symbol inventory and caller context, not coverage of their files.
